$comment: Single owner of the frontmatter fields recognized by the Claude Code runtime. Read by .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java in `schema` mode. Add a field HERE, never in the Java. Design and rationale: .claude/decisions/0001-schema-frontmatter-extensions.md

injections.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `schema`, applied to every file that mode already visits. A `!`command`` injection runs in the session's persistent shell, at whatever cwd it holds: a `cd` in an earlier Bash call makes a relative `test -f` report a file as absent while it exists, and an injected state that lies fires the entry guard of the skill it belongs to. Requiring the substring below is deliberately blunt — an injection that touches no path at all is also flagged, because `ls -a | head -30` was one of the twelve real occurrences and names no path either. Scope and escapes, each one a false positive the first run produced: only files a `types` match captures are scanned (a decision record or a lessons-learned is prose about injections, and `schema` is handed one on every Edit under .claude/); a fenced code block is dropped; and so is a double-backtick span, which is how markdown has to quote an injection when documenting it. `exempt_patterns` is the escape hatch, one regex per genuinely cwd-independent injection; it is empty on purpose, and an entry added to it needs a reason in the commit. Why this is a hook and not a review item: CLAUDE.md invariant 6. Design: .claude/decisions/0051-frontmatter-injections-cwd-independent.md

audit.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `audit` mode. The audited set is not listed here: any name that resolves to .claude/skills/<n>/SKILL.md or .claude/agents/<n>.md is recorded, invoked by `/command` or by the model's own Skill/Agent call. Not frontmatter: it lives here because this file is the single owner of every list the hook reads. `redact` runs before the initial prompt is written into the versioned .claude/audit-usage/ report — each `patterns` entry MUST expose the key part as group 1, the replacement keeps $1 and blanks the rest. `exclude_skills` names the skills that carry `disable-model-invocation: true`, and so would be audited, but that OBSERVE instead of producing work — `audit-usage` reads the trail, `arch-doctor` reads the setup. Invoking one closes the run in progress and opens none of its own. Closing was already what happened (any second `/command` closes), so this only drops the empty report an observer would otherwise leave behind; the gain is that a report read mid-session is finished rather than stuck at `⏳ em andamento`. For `audit-usage` it also breaks a feedback loop: reading the trail would append a report about reading, and the next read would be mostly reads. Design: .claude/decisions/0035-auditoria-execucao-hook.md, .claude/decisions/0036-skill-audit-usage.md and .claude/decisions/0038-audit-trail-every-skill-and-agent.md

guard.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `guard` mode, wired only into project-bootstrap/templates/settings.json.example. While a design skill runs (opened by `/<skill>` or a Skill call to one of `design_skills`, closed by the next prompt or by an `executor_agents` Agent call), Write/Edit on `design_forbidden_paths` is blocked unless the call comes from inside an executor agent. Independently, any file under `use_cases_dir`/UC-*/ whose UC-*-spec.md has a status in `frozen_statuses` is blocked, except the executor's single Edit of `status: approved` to `status: implemented`. Why: a design skill once wrote migrations under src/, and a later use case rewrote the specs of an earlier one — both while the skills forbade it in prose.

mcp.$comment: Validated by ArchHook.java schema, same as `types` above. Design: .claude/decisions/0033-mcp-in-architect-designer.md
